Abstract

Natural language call routing can be treated as an instance of text categorization of documents after the speech of the calls has been recognized. This categorization consists of two important parts. The first part is text preprocessing for numerical data extraction and the second part is the classification with machine learning. In this paper we will present how to perform text preprocessing for numerical data extraction, and then we classify the calls with different machine learning algorithms, and evaluate the performance of each algorithm. We found that Support Vector Machines (SVM) and k-nearest neighbors (KNN) performed better than Naive Bayes (NB), Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), and Random Forest (RF). We also find that the Levenshtein edit distance performs better than Jaccard and Cosine similarity.
